thought.text: Confirmed: **backend health `{"status":"UP"}`** ✓. The cms dev server was OOM-killed (the 7.6GB machine can't hold 3 Angular dev servers + 10 containers). Two frontends (app, boards) are running. Let me start cms now (its build is cached → low memory) and check whether all three fit:

reasoning_content:
Confirmed:
- **Backend health: `{"groups":["liveness","readiness"],"status":"UP"}`** ✓
- The CMS development server was **killed by OOM** (dmesg: "Out of memory: Killed process ... anon-rss:2146144kB") — the 7.6GB machine cannot run 3 Angular development servers + 10 containers simultaneously.

This is a clear **resource constraint of the environment**, not a defect in the installation. Each frontend works standalone and sequentially. The last one that was started (or the one being built) gets killed by OOM.

Now, as the final state, all three are needed simultaneously. The problem is: the running servers each hold about 1.3–2GB, plus the containers take about 2.5GB, and the machine only has 7.6GB. 3 servers ≈ 4.5GB + containers 2.5GB = 7GB > 7.6GB → OOM occurs when all 3 are running.

The OOM killer killed the most recent one (cms). Let's reduce the memory of the running servers. Actually, in the steady state after the build, each Vite server uses about 300–500MB. The problem was that the boards build (about 2GB peak) was running while app and cms were running.

Let's verify: right now app (39001) and boards (39003) are running (both 200). cms got killed. If I start cms now (build already cached, low memory), will it fit?

Let me check the current memory usage of the 2 running servers + containers.

action.command:
echo "=== current memory by component ==="; free -m | sed -n '2p'
ps aux --sort=-rss | grep -E "run-executor|esbuild|java|node" | grep -v grep | awk '{printf "pid=%s rss=%sMB %s\n",$2,int($6/1024),$11}' | head -12
